SOURCE-ASSISTED SELECTED READING (batch of 12 October 2026, second pass)

Base: batch-2026-10-12-image-only. Made after the candidate was known, with Bremen, SuUB, msa 0137, f. 27v to hand. Span A was read on the fragment tile and on the Bremen page image by the coordinator, after a research reader; spans B and C are the research reader's, not rechecked word for word. Parentheses expand abbreviations; square brackets mark text lost (holes) or not read; a question mark follows an uncertain reading.

A. Canvas "fol. [1]v, upper board", native-pixel box 121,1227,1210,2362. Physical lines from the top of that box:
1: [...] no(n) [...]
2: re ip(su)m irrevo(ca)b(i)l(ite)r fuisse ligatu(m). e. sollicitudine(m).
3: [S]i post app(e)ll(ati)o(n)em redit a[d d]elegatu(m) ex. [...] del.
4: g(ra)tu(m). ex. [de] testi. cu(m) v[e]nisse(n)t? Secus in ord[inario] [...]
5: si al(iqui)s app(e)llavit ad p(a)p(a)m et postea rediit ad ordinari-
6: u(m) p(ro) alia ca(usa) s(upe)r q(ua) no(n) app(e)llavit no(n) p(er) h(oc) videt(ur) renu(n)-
7: ciasse app(e)ll(ati)o(n)i cu(m) ille adhu[c iu]dex suus ordinari(us)
8: in aliis ca(us)is sit. e. cu(m) tenea(mur). q(ua)n(do) a(u)t(em) app(e)ll(atu)r a de-
9: legato tu(n)c nulla remanet ei iu(r)isd(i)c(ti)o. e. ut debitus.
10: [U]n(de) si redit ad delegatu(m) renu(n)ciare videtur app(e)l-
11: lat(i)o(n)i. Jo. In. si exco(mmun)icatur ab aliquo iudice app(e)l-
12: lans petit absolut(i)o(n)em cu(m) p(ro)test(ati)o(n)e q(uo)d salva sit s(ibi)
13: app(e)llat(i)o no(n) videtur renu(n)ciasse app(e)ll(ation)i cu(m) i(n) ea sit
14: p(er)ic(u)l(u)m. ex. de sen. ex. sac(r)o. s(ed) si sine p(ro)test(ati)o(n)e peter(et)
15: absolvi renu(n)ciare videtur. alii dicunt q(uo)d iudex
16: a quo app(e)llavit nu(m)q(uam) p(otes)t absolv(er)e n(is)i appellans re-
17: nu(n)ciet app(e)ll(ation)i.
18: [Q](ua)n(do) (com)positione(m) acceptat? ex. de el. cu(m) int(er). Jo.
19: [S]i aliquis i(n) ca(usa) app(e)ll(ati)o(n)is vadit ad arbitros no(n) p(ro)p(ter)
Line 18: the research reader read "Qui compositionem attemptat"; the Bremen manuscript has "Quando compositionem acceptat", which the letters here also allow.

B. Same canvas, continuing below (tile from native 121,2142; research reader):
... hoc renuntiavit appellationi immo postea potest prosequi appellationem nec currit ei tempus interim. C. de temp. ap. In aut. si tamen. hoc b. ex. de renun. veniens. Si aliquis appellavit a sententia et postea solvit id in quo condempnatus fuit si hoc fecit [ne]cessitate iudicis tunc repetere potest solutum tamquam indebitum si in causa appellationis pro ipso sententiatum fuit. sponte sic non potest repetere quia videtur renuntiasse appellationi. ff. e. cum ex causa. in tex. et in glo. Jo.

C. Canvas "fol. [1]r", right column, foot, native-pixel box about 1050,2230,2076,3100 (research reader):
... quod appellationi renuntiat. Qui post appellationem agit vel respondet vel producit testes ex. de testi. cum venissent. contra ex. de eo qui mit. in pos. cum venissent ubi reus appellaverat et iudex nolens deferre appellationi misit actorem in possessionem rei petite causa custodie et reus postea infra annum obtulit cautionem sisti iuri sed actor noluit illam recipere et mandat papa quod cognoscatur utrum appellatio fuit legitima ... ergo talem offerendo cautionem non renuntiavit appellationi sue. Responsio hoc ideo est secundum b. quia adversarius noluit recipere cautionem ...

Corrections to the first reading from the comparison: "necessitate iudicis"; "Responsio: hoc ideo est secundum b."; "hoc b.".
